acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: A verdict with an empty checklist or an empty acceptance list is rejected by the schema, by the transport schema, and by enforce_cca_verdict with a precise reason.
An unusable generation is retried inside the same run, bounded, and a well-formed one never is.
The three suites whose fixtures encode an empty checklist are updated so each still proves the property it was written for.
The full suite, the evidence-integrity, guardian-policy, control-plane and governance-evidence suites and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: It happened. On PR #233 the CCA emitted a verdict with ZERO checklist entries and ZERO acceptance entries. It was caught downstream by a MergeGate rule ('CCA verdict acceptance evidence is empty'), not by the schema — the verdict was schema-VALID. `.shiki/schemas/cca-verdict.schema.json` declares checklist and acceptance as arrays with no minItems, and the transport schema the workflow passes to `--json-schema` has no minItems either, so nothing at any layer required the judge to judge anything.

The blast radius of adding minItems was MEASURED, not estimated. With `minItems: 1` on both arrays: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → 691 tests, OK. `validate_shiki` → passed. `scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh` → passed (its deliberately-empty fixtures do not go through schema validation). Exactly THREE suites fail, each on a fixture that hardcodes an empty checklist: test_shiki_evidence_integrity.sh (lines 56, 267), test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh (line 434) and test_shiki_control_plane.sh (lines 280, 765, 1325). Line 280's failure is instructive: it asserts the message 'repair_required verdict must include a non-null object', and with minItems the fixture now fails for the schema reason instead, so the grep misses. Those three files are therefore in the locks, and nothing else is.

The only verdict-shaped record in the mirror with an empty checklist is `.shiki/templates/CCA_VERDICT.template.json`, which is a template rather than a mirror record and is not covered by validate_shiki's schema-conformance loop. No recorded verdict has to be rewritten.

Schema tightening alone is not enough. It converts a degenerate verdict from 'accepted' into 'the run fails', which is correct but still costs a full `gh run rerun`. And a partial `gh run rerun --failed` does NOT help: it reuses the previous job's artifact, so the stale degenerate verdict comes back. That was measured on #233 — the partial re-run reproduced the failure and only a full re-run regenerated the verdict.

The retry belongs inside the run, bounded, and only for verdicts that are UNUSABLE — absent, unparseable, or degenerate. A verdict that judged the PR and returned repair_required or needs_guardian is a real answer and must never be retried; retrying a real answer until it changes would be judge-shopping, which is exactly what a completion gate must not do.
grill_with_docs.source: Measured 2026-08-01 against main at c0082fe, plus live operation on PR #233 on 2026-07-31.

non_goals: Retrying a well-formed verdict of any value, including repair_required, needs_guardian, blocked or insufficient_evidence.
Changing verdict semantics, the checklist ids, or docs/agents/checklists.md.
Changing what MergeGate does with a well-formed verdict.
Rewriting any recorded verdict in the mirror.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: A CCA verdict that judged nothing can no longer be emitted, accepted, or recorded, and a single unusable generation no longer costs a full manual re-run. The two are the same defect seen from both ends: the schema permits a verdict with an empty checklist, and when the model produces one there is no recovery inside the run.
title: Refuse a degenerate CCA verdict and stop losing a whole run to one bad generation
